teams.heading: Warren Gatland says he chose not to apply for Fiji job
teams.body: Former Wales head coach Warren Gatland says he spoke with Fiji about the role before deciding not to apply, with Jake White now in the job ahead of next year's World Cup. Gatland, who also declined a Harlequins offer earlier in the year on timing, has a verdict on the appointment: "Jake White will do a good job." Fiji's first Test under White is Saturday against Japan.

lead.why: Gatland's disclosure that he spoke with Fiji about the coaching job before withdrawing is new, and it is a Fiji coaching story rather than the squad news already run.

teams.heading: Northampton back George Hendy says he is serious about an England call-up
teams.body: Northampton back George Hendy is pressing his claims for England, saying he would take a spot on the wing or at 15 if it gets him into the squad. "I just want to throw my hat in the ring for England and I'm really quite serious about that," the 24-year-old told BBC Sport. He has scored 44 tries in 80 games for Northampton, and England boss Steve Borthwick names a training squad on Sunday for the November Nations Championship matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand in London.

lead.why: It is a new item about an England hopeful ahead of Borthwick's training squad, which is the national-side selection story the shortlist offers today.

teams.heading: Gregory Alldritt recalled to France squad after year away under Galthié
teams.body: Gregory Alldritt is back in Fabien Galthié's France squad for the November Nations Championship matches, a year after he last featured. The La Rochelle number eight, 29, has 58 caps and captained Les Bleus against Australia in November 2025 in Antoine Dupont's absence, but fell out of favour and was sidelined in July with a calf injury. Galthié also named seven newcomers in his 42-man squad, and Alldritt is in contention for the second part of the Nations Championship, which includes South Africa on 13 November in Paris.

lead.why: A fresh squad story about a senior France player's return, distinct from Friday's Ward call-up already reported.

teams.heading: Neve Jones to win 50th cap as Ireland women face South Africa
teams.body: Ireland women's hooker Neve Jones will win her 50th cap on Saturday, the 17th Irish woman to reach the half-century, as head coach Scott Bemand makes just two changes for the first WXV Global Series Test against South Africa. Jones starts for the third game in a row, between props Linda Djougang and Eilís Cahill. Stacey Flood returns at full-back and Dorothy Wall comes back into the second row from the side that beat Japan 43-19 in Cork.

lead.why: It is the newest story in the shortlist, and Neve Jones' 50th cap is a clear personal milestone for an Ireland fan, even though it is the women's side.

teams.heading: Italy average 28.9 points conceded across their last 11 games
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Italy have scored 190 points, an average of 17.3 a game. Across the same stretch they have conceded 318, an average of 28.9. Their best result in that window was a 34-19 home win over Chile in November 2025, in International Friendlies. Their next fixture is South Africa in the Nations Championship, the reigning world champions.

teams.heading: Aicha Sutcliffe makes first Scotland women's start against Australia
teams.body: Scotland women's hooker Aicha Sutcliffe makes her first start for the side, one of three changes made by interim head coach Dave Butcher for Friday's final WXV Global Series match against Australia. Glasgow Warriors' Sutcliffe already has six caps off the bench, and Harlequins lock Sarah Bonar returns to the second row after missing the 56-12 defeat to Australia through illness. Scotland lost the earlier meeting 30-10 and are still seeking a first win in this season's competition.

lead.why: The only fresh Scotland item in the pack that is not already reported, and it is tied to today's match.

teams.heading: Wales women's Alex Callender to win 50th cap against Japan Saturday
teams.body: Wales women's flanker Alex Callender will win her 50th cap in Saturday's WXV Global Series game against Japan. Callender, who won her first cap in 2019, is co-captain with Kate Williams and has returned from injuries suffered before, during and after the 2025 World Cup. Sisters Nel and Branwen Metcalfe also start their first Test together. Lynn said: "Whenever she puts that jersey on she wears it with pride and wants to represent the nation."

lead.why: A fresh, match-pinned item that is distinct from the Lake injury and the uncapped-trio selection already run.

teams.heading: Argentina's biggest win in their last 11 games: 52-28 over Wales
teams.body: Argentina's biggest win across their last 11 games was a 52-28 away victory over Wales in November 2025, filed under International Friendlies, and it is the win that stands out in that window. Their most recent result was a 28-28 draw with Australia. The Pumas take that Wales scoreline into their next fixture, Ireland v Argentina in Round 4 of the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Victor Matfield says Wallabies are 'definitely not top four' after Bledisloe losses
teams.body: Former Springboks lock Victor Matfield doubts Australia are even a top-five side, and thinks they will not reach the semi-finals of next year's home Rugby World Cup. Asked where the Wallabies sit, his answer was an emphatic no: "They're definitely not top four. I don't even think top five." Australia are seventh on the World Rugby rankings after back-to-back Bledisloe Cup defeats to New Zealand, the first two losses of the Les Kiss era. Ex-All Blacks winger Sir John Kirwan, reviewing the second Bledisloe defeat, said he "just can't get a read" on the side.

lead.why: Fresh, talked-about verdict on where the Wallabies stand, and it isn't the referee appointment already covered today.

teams.heading: Japan women's XV start Savannah Bodman and Sophie Akiko Langford against Wales
teams.body: Japan's women's XV open the first of two WXV Global Series Tests against Wales on Saturday with Savannah Bodman at number 8 and Sophie Akiko Langford at outside centre. Head coach Toshizumi Kitagawa, whose tenure has included losses to Fiji, Italy and twice to Ireland, has picked a squad willing to blood new players. Wales lead the head-to-head 2-0, including a 19-10 win at WXV2 in 2024.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item; the men's Fiji story is the Deans piece already run, so this women's selection story is labelled and led instead.

teams.heading: Sir Graham Henry says All Blacks learned to train at Test intensity
teams.body: Former All Blacks coach Sir Graham Henry, now a national selector under Dave Rennie, says the squad's biggest lesson from the South Africa tour is how they train. Players must practise at Test intensity and physicality, a standard that risks injury but is needed to deliver on the weekend, he says. He also cited a Lions fixture in Johannesburg between the first and second Tests as a partial excuse, and admitted the adjustment will take time.

lead.why: A new item on the current national squad's training after the South Africa tour, from a selector with direct access to the group.

teams.heading: Springbok Women brace for physical Ireland test after inconsistent WXV
teams.body: South Africa's women host Ireland in the first of two WXV Global Series Tests this weekend, and Ireland captain Erin King expects the physical battle to decide it. The Springbok Women have been inconsistent, with wins over Spain and Italy offset by a heavy defeat to Wales, while Ireland opened with a loss to the USA. King says Ireland "definitely don't shy away from" the physicality, and it is Ireland's first women's Test on Springbok soil.

lead.why: The only new item about South Africa in the shortlist that is not already covered, and it is labelled as the women's side.
